payload.description:
## Trigger

When a repository installs a kit standalone it gets working code and nothing that tells an agent the code exists, so the agent never calls it, and I want each kit to ship its own skill and the instruction that triggers it, so a consumer without basicly gets the behaviour and not just the binary.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-12, on the kit distribution landing: "the kit is not complete as it does not ship the dedicated skill at the least and instructions on how and when to call the skill in always-on instructions or at least scoped on when a coding file is created and edited, and a way on how to add this info to always-on instruction files if basicly is not installed in that repo. And this is also valid for all kits! Otherwise how would an agent in a consumer repo without basicly know when to use model tier and how, and when and how to use the work tracker."

The point is exact. `basicly-ssbkq5c` was written as an installer record and its acceptance criteria are all about files, attributes and idempotence. Every one of them is met and the kit is still not usable by an agent, because in this repository the guidance arrives through a channel the standalone install does not carry: fragments and skills projected by `basicly build`. A consumer who never runs `basicly` has neither.

## Measured, 2026-09-12

- Three kits ship: `comments`, `tracker`, `tier`. Each install writes only `.py` files, a README and, for the tracker, two git rules.
- Guidance for the comment ban exists in this repository as the `code-is-authoritative` fragment (path-scoped) and in the `python-guidelines` skill. **Neither travels with the kit.**
- Guidance for the tier kit is the `tier-injection` skill; for the tracker it is the `work-tracker` skill. **Neither travels either.**
- So a consumer repository that runs `basicly-comments init` has a hook-ready checker and no agent instruction anywhere that a comment is refused.

## Acceptance Criteria

- EACH KIT SHALL carry its own agent skill in its own directory, authored so it is not discoverable as a skill inside this repository.
- THE INSTALL SHALL write that skill into the agent skill roots a consumer actually reads, and `uninstall` SHALL remove exactly what it wrote.
- EACH KIT SHALL carry a short always-on block stating when to reach for the skill, and the install SHALL make it available to a repository that has no basicly.
- WHERE the consumer has an always-on instruction file, THE INSTALL SHALL be able to write that block into it inside a marked, idempotent region that `uninstall` removes, and SHALL NOT do so silently by default.
- WHERE the consumer has no such file, THE INSTALL SHALL print the block so a human can place it.
- THE SKILL AND THE BLOCK SHALL be the same text this repository uses, read from one source rather than written twice.
- A TEST SHALL install each kit into a throwaway repository, assert the skill and the block land where an agent reads them, and assert `uninstall` returns the tree to its original state.

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- depends on: `basicly-ssbkq5c` (closed)
- demonstration: in a throwaway repository with no basicly, install each kit and show the agent-facing files that appeared, then uninstall and show the tree is as it started
payload.title: each kit ships the skill and the instruction that make an agent use it

payload.description:
## Retro proposal, not applied

Session 2026-09-12. Awaiting the owner decision.

## The gap
`tests/test_kit_packages.py` proves two things and not the third. Two tests build a wheel and assert its `namelist()` carries the kit and the installer. Twenty-eight tests call `installer.run(...)` against the source module. Nothing installs a wheel and executes `init` from it.

So the packaging is checked and the logic is checked, and the join between them is not. A shim that cannot locate its kit at runtime, a `force-include` mapping that lands files at the wrong module path, an entry point that does not resolve - each would pass every test and break every consumer.

## How it surfaced
Only by hand. `uvx --from <wheel> basicly-tier init` in a scratch repository was the sole thing that exercised the path, and it is what proved both that the kits work and that the third skill copy was being written.

## Proposal
One test per kit: build the wheel, `uvx --from <wheel> basicly-<kit> init --into <tmp>` in a throwaway git repository, and assert the vendored kit, the two skill roots and the exit code. Slow, so mark it and keep it in `full` rather than `fast`.

## Why this and not more source-level tests
The source-level suite is already thorough. The defect class it cannot see is precisely the one that only appears once the wheel is built and installed, which is the state every consumer is in and no test was.

## Scope
- `tests/test_kit_packages.py`
- `basicly.toml`
payload.title: No test runs a kit installer the way a consumer runs it

payload.text:
EVIDENCE FOR THIS PROPOSAL 2026-09-16: the procedure it asks for was run four times by hand today and **found two real defects that every existing test missed**.

The procedure: `uv build --wheel packages/basicly-tier`, then `uvx --from <wheel> basicly-tier init` into a fresh `git init` directory with no `.basicly/core`, then exercise the vendored copy, then `uninstall`.

DEFECT ONE, invisible to the 28 source-module tests. `claude_tier_hook` called `find_map(cwd, beside_the_kit=False)`, which searches only `<base><redacted:posix-absolute-path>`. A standalone consumer has no `.basicly/core`, so the hook found no map and **silently declined every rewrite**. Every source-module test ran inside this repository, where the catalog map exists, so none of them could see it.

DEFECT TWO, also invisible. `uninstall` removed the vendored files and left the `PreToolUse`/`Agent` entry pointing at a deleted path. Only a full install-then-uninstall against a real wheel shows it.

The first fix attempt then introduced a third defect the same way: scoping the map fallback to the ancestor walk made a kit in one repository answer for a sibling repository under the same parent. A negative test caught that one before it landed.

So the join between packaging and logic is not theoretical. It is where three defects lived today. The manual runs are recorded on basicly-a3yi; what is still missing is that any of this is a **test**, which is exactly what this record proposes.

BUILT 2026-09-16, commit dec851c2. `tests/test_kit_consumer_install.py`, five tests, 1.6s.

The gap this record named - "Nothing installs a wheel and executes `init` from it" - is closed. Each test builds a real wheel with `uv build --wheel` and drives it with `uvx --from <wheel> basicly-<kit>` against a fresh `git init` directory.

- All three kits install from their own wheel and land a vendored tree and a skill.
- The tier kit wires the `PreToolUse`/`Agent` hook and its vendored hook resolves `tier: low` to `haiku` **in a repository with no `.basicly/core` at all**, which is asserted as the control so a green result cannot come from this repository's own catalog.
- Uninstall from the wheel leaves no `Agent` hook naming a deleted kit.

Those last two assertions are the two defects the manual runs found earlier the same day, now pinned so they cannot return.

## Context

Found by the lane-B survey 2026-08-14, with a measured dependency scan. `basicly-tcmy.13` owns the split. This names where to cut.

Cross-section edge counts, from an abstract syntax tree walk between the section headers:

```text
section                 lines        inbound edges    prose share
lock and heartbeat      108-310      2                36.9%
outcome routing         2810-3905    0                45.2%
usage meter             978-1158     1                34.2%
telemetry and dispatch  2077-2809    6                48.5%
```

## Why routing goes first

It is a pure dependency sink. Zero inbound references means no symbol in `supervise` needs a forwarding shim. It consumes only the lane outcome, the session state, the found-info record, the ready set, and the `merge`, `loop`, `decisions` and `policy` modules.

The two nameable halves are admit and dispatch a pass, and route and land the outcomes.

## The meter goes second

After the cycle is thinned, the meter at 978-1158 is the only thing `loop` reaches in `supervise`. Extracting it is what removes the layering exemption.

## The ratchet arithmetic

Routing at 45.2% prose sits above the module mean of 43.6%, so extracting it lowers the remainder's share. Both sides sit under the cap on a line-based measure. Re-measure with the gate's own token-based script before the commit, because `supervise.py` is frozen at 55.9.

## Warning

`tests/test_supervise.py` is frozen at 60,132 tokens. Move the routing tests out with the code or the test module's own ratchet blocks the lane.

## Acceptance

- When the routing section is extracted, then no forwarding shim is added to `supervise`.
- When both size gates run, then no baseline is raised and `supervise.py` shrinks in the same diff.
- When a supervised pass runs, then its routed outcomes are unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- a new module
- `.importlinter`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

## Depends on

The thinning of the loop to supervise cycle.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_supervise.py -q`, both ratchet scripts, and `uv run lint-imports`.

## Context

Step 6, the residue after `basicly-s5li` moves the 26 `comments` sites to ledger events.
Measured 2026-08-07 by enumerating every `_run_br` call site in `src/basicly/`.

55 sites total. `comments` is 26 of them and is `s5li`. This bead is the other 29, and
the finding is that they fall into four classes of very different cost - a quarter of
them delete themselves.

## Class 1 - the ledger already models these (11 sites)

Each maps onto an event kind `events.py` already declares:

| Call | Sites | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update -t <type>`, `update --external-ref` | `classify.py:54`, `loop.py:370`, `loop.py:1994` | `field` |
| `close --reason` | `loop.py:433` | `status` |
| `dep add -t blocks` | `supervise.py:899`, `supervise.py:1043`, `decompose.py:2056`, `merge.py:1117` | `edge` |
| `dep cycles --blocking-only` | `decompose.py:2019` | derived from `edge` |
| `create` | `supervise.py:1041`, `decompose.py:1815` | `created` |

Note `edge` is already in the ledger - the step-1 import wrote 658 of them - but `fsck`
reports it as an unfolded kind because the fold applies no state for it and a sibling
module derives it directly. Folding `edge` is a prerequisite for answering `blocked` and
`dep cycles` from the ledger.

## Class 2 - the ledger can already answer these (4 sites)

`show --json` (`br.py:1159`, `decompose.py:1988`) is **already flipped** at `MODE_OWNED`
via `read_record`. `blocked --json` (`loop_state.py:308`) and `dep cycles` derive from
folded edges. `gate list --robot` (`policy.py:424`) reads gate records, which are
`[harness-policy]` markers and therefore land with `s5li` rather than here.

## Class 3 - these disappear when br does (4 sites)

They exist only to serve br and have no owned equivalent to build:

- `sync --merge`, `sync --flush-only` (`merge.py:466`, `merge.py:520`) - br database to
  JSONL reconciliation. No second store, no sync.
- `init --prefix` (`cli.py:924`) - creates a br tracker.
- `where --json` (`worktree.py:208`) - probes the `.beads/redirect` file, which exists so
  a worktree shares the base checkout br database.

Deleting these is the measurable end of the dependency, not a migration.

## Class 4 - the one open question (1 site)

`br lint --json` (`policy.py:195`) feeds the Definition-of-Ready. It is br validating a
bead body shape, not a fact about our work graph. Decide deliberately: reimplement the
shape check we actually rely on, or drop it and let the DoR sections gate alone. Do not
port it by reflex - `required_sections` already encodes what the DoR needs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the engine at tracker mode owned with br absent from PATH when a bead is created or typed or closed or given an edge and when the ready set and blocked set and dependency cycles are computed then every one succeeds from the ledger alone and the four br-only call sites named in class 3 no longer exist in src

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/classify.py`
